thread:
amelia: hey team — I just joined (hi 👋). I'm on infra and trying to get access to Vault + our KMS for a sandbox service, but I'm stuck. When I try to read secrets I get permission denied. Can someone point me to the minimal steps to request access and how rotation works?

samir: welcome, Amelia! quick checklist so you can get unblocked: 1) open an access request via the onboarding portal, 2) attach the service account + repo + env, 3) request 'secrets/read' role for Vault path(s), 4) request KMS decrypt for the key ring. I'll paste the exact fields below. :thumbsup:

samir: request template (copy into the portal):
```
- Name: Amelia T. (new-hi)
- Team: infra
- Service account: infra-svc-acct@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- Vault paths: secret/data/infra/sandbox, secret/data/infra/common
- KMS: projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/sandbox
- Reason: dev sandbox and debugging
- Duration: 90d (temporary)
```

samir: after you submit, eng-security will approve or request clarification. They usually create a scoped token and annotate the request with rotation policy (monthly or 90d) depending on env.

amelia: thanks — do you know if I need GCP IAM role beforehand for the KMS request?

samir: yes, add roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the service account for that key. If you don't have permissions to grant that, just note it in the portal request and security will grant it for you.

jordan: FYI for local dev: don't use real prod secrets. Use the dev-only secret backend: `secret/data/dev/*` or the local secrets manager (`dev-secrets` CLI). To pull a dev secret: `redwood-dev secrets get infra/sandbox --env=local` — this returns a wrapped value you can unwrap with the dev KMS.

infra-bot: new access request created: #SR-4567 by amelia. Current status: pending — eng-security queue. Link: https://onboard.redwood.com/requests/SR-4567

onboarding-bot: Hi @amelia — welcome again! Quick pointers: docs: https://docs.redwood.com/security/secrets, vault onb: https://docs.redwood.com/security/secrets/onboarding, rotation: https://docs.redwood.com/security/secrets/rotation

amelia: super helpful — one more question: what triggers rotation and how are apps affected? If a key rotates, do we need to redeploy?

samir: good question. short answer: KMS/CMEK rotations are automated for customer-managed keys on a monthly cadence for prod; Vault secrets rotate according to the secret engine policy (can be hourly/daily/monthly). apps using envelope encryption should continue to read older ciphertexts until keys are retired — but if you pin a specific key version you'll need to update. Most Redwood services rely on key version aliasing so no redeploy is required. For manual steps: 1) security rotates key, 2) old key is set to disabled after 7d, 3) data owner may re-encrypt active data if necessary.

samir: TL;DR — usually no redeploy, but double-check if your service caches the raw key id or key version at startup. If it does, add a watch to refresh the key info from metadata endpoint.

jordan: addition: avoid embedding KMS key ids or plaintext secrets in code or container images. use the secrets client with short-lived tokens.

amelia: thanks everyone. I'll submit the portal request now and drop the SR here once it's up. Appreciate the fast help!

infra-bot: SR-4567 updated: approved by eng-security, ACLs will be applied in ~15m.

amelia: confirmed I can read the two dev paths now. closing the loop — thanks :raised_hands:

samir: great — welcome aboard! ping me if you want a walkthrough of rotation policies or the vault audit logs.

jordan: also happy to pair on local dev secret setup tomorrow.

amelia: that would be great — i'll DM to schedule.
